text:
carmen: Quick sync — following the RFC, I want to propose an adaptive smoke layer that picks production-like samples for a tiny replay instead of fixed seeds. idea: more realistic surface checks without full bench cost.
dev: interesting. you mean sample from recent request traces (sanitized) and run 100 replays? :thinking_face: would need privacy handling.
carmen: yes, strip PII, only keep token ids & lengths. pick buckets by route/template so we cover common prompt shapes.
rahul: two concerns: (1) reproducibility of golden comparisons, (2) flakiness if prod traffic has noisy templates.
carmen: for reproducibility we maintain a 'golden snapshot' per bucket refreshed weekly. the smoke will compare distributional metrics (token shift, top-5 overlap) rather than exact logits.
esther: metric suggestions: top5_overlap_pct, js_divergence_on_probs (small sample), p95_latency, mem_peak. define thresholds per bucket since chat differs from short-completion.
dev: policy mode: fail/block only on manifest/tokenizer/oom. for distributional regressions -> warn and throttle rollout. we can't block for subtle semantic drift.
carmen: agreed. blocklist for hard fails: missing kv layout, tokenizer id mismatches, model fails to load within X sec, OOM. Everything else is advisory.
rahul: how do we record these in model registry? keep metadata flat. propose keys: smoke.status (pass/warn/fail), smoke.metrics (comma-separated), smoke.bucket_ids (pipe-separated), smoke.report_url.
esther: + add smoke.run_ts and smoke.runner. store runner as string "smoke-v1". keep artifacts as list of strings for report links.
dev: runner implementation: sampler service emits sanitized batches to a queue, smoke-runner picks up with config: --buckets=a,b,c --max-samples=120 --golden-age=7d. Runner should run CPU-first and escalate to GPU if load fails.
rahul: add replay isolation: run in chroot with network off except for pulling model weights, which must be pre-cached. prevent models that fetch external assets from leaking. default timeout 45s for pulls.
carmen: rollout idea: newly ingested models start in 'canary_soft' with 0.5% traffic and smoke must complete within N hours else auto-throttle to 0.01%. if smoke warns -> keep soft and alert SEs. if smoke fails -> block promotion.
esther: also add an automatic re-run trigger: any time production trace sampling shows >2x JS divergence vs golden, schedule immediate smoke re-run. helps catch regressions post-deploy.
dev: ops note: rate-limit per org: 3 concurrent smoke runs standard, bumpable for enterprise. also add backpressure if many models requeue.
rahul: cost estimate: ~0.02 GPU-hours per smoke if GPU needed, else minimal. include budget tag in registry: smoke.allocated_quota=standard/enterprise.
carmen: CLI example for docs:
```
redwood-smoke run --model $MID --buckets chat-short,completion-long --samples 120 --fast --output gs://bench/smoke/123.json
```
Report schema (brief): smoke.status=warn, smoke.metrics="p95:28.5,p99:42.2,mem:1.6GB,top5:0.81,js:0.06", smoke.artifacts=["gs://bench/smoke/123.json"], smoke.run_ts=1797622222
dev: make sure onboarding UI surfaces smoke.status and gives a clear next-step for SEs (re-run, escalate, accept-with-warning). also audit when human override is used.
esther: add retention policy: keep smoke artifacts for 30d; golden snapshots 90d. store pointers in registry metadata only.
rahul: one more ask: for models that are quantized variants, smoke should validate that KV cache behavior matches fp baseline for a small set; otherwise flag for manual review.
carmen: good catch. we'll add kv_consistency check that compares a cached prefix replay. small footprint.
onboard-bot: smoke queue provisioned. docs stub: https://internal.redwood/onboard/adaptive-smoke. scheduled job will reconcile every 10m.
carmen: i'll write the follow-up doc with schema, buckets proposal, and a sample rollout plan. will ping @dev and @esther for review. :memo:
